description: Go ecosystem (gomod). Ties the Go toolchain together: the golang Docker image, go.mod's `go`/`toolchain` directives and setup-go's `go-version:` input move as ONE `go toolchain` PR, and the `go` directive actually bumps (under the fleet's `rangeStrategy: pin` it never does). Go MINORS (1.27 -> 1.28) are reviewed like majors; patches automerge. Indirect modules are tracked, `golang.org/x/*` moves as one group, and every gomod update runs `go mod tidy`. Extend AFTER :automerge and BEFORE :docker, like :python. TOP-LEVEL `postUpdateOptions`: every gomod update runs `go mod tidy` and, on a module major (`/v2` -> `/v3`), rewrites import paths so the PR compiles. Top level ON PURPOSE, not in a gomod-scoped packageRule: `postUpdateOptions` is `mergeable`, so preset and consumer lists concatenate, and artifact steps read the BRANCH config, which `generateBranchConfig` builds from `upgrades[0]` after sorting by depName. A gomod-only rule would apply only when a gomod upgrade happens to sort first: a `go toolchain` branch led by setup-go's `go` dep, or an npm+go bundle led by an npm dep, would skip tidy. Only the gomod artifact step reads `gomod*` options, so no other manager is affected.

packageRules.description: Track indirect modules. Renovate's gomod extractor disables every `// indirect` require by default, but that is where the CVEs land: owine/labelprint's only direct module (zebrash) pins golang.org/x/image and x/text, and the image's Trivy HIGH/CRITICAL gate failed on both (CVE-2026-46603, CVE-2026-56851/56852) before OSV flagged them for Renovate. Requiring a newer version in go.mod overrides the dependency's floor (minimal version selection), so an indirect bump is a real, shipped change and keeps the `deps:` baseline. Fully enabled rather than Renovate's `security:gomodIndirectSecurityUpdates` (security-only): Trivy can see a CVE before OSV does, and a security-only rule waits for OSV. Non-major bumps ride automerge.json's bundle (or `golang-x` below), so the extra churn costs no review.

Force `rangeStrategy: bump` for go.mod's `go` directive, or it NEVER moves. gomod extracts it with `go-mod-directive` versioning, which reads `go 1.27.3` as the range `^1.27.3` and returns a new value only under `bump`. Under `replace` it keeps the current value while the new release still satisfies that range (every 1.x), and under anything else, including default.json's top-level `rangeStrategy: pin`, it always keeps it. No update, no warning, no dashboard entry, and the `go toolchain` group below silently carries only the image. Measured on Renovate 44.201.0: a `go 1.26.1` fixture produced nothing under fleet defaults and `1.26.1 -> 1.27.3` with this rule (the same class of trap as alpine.json's apk `replace`). `bump` writes the full `X.Y.Z` for any Go >= 1.20, so `go 1.22` becomes `go 1.27.3`. Scoped to depType `golang`: the `toolchain` directive uses semver versioning and already updates under `pin`.

golang.org/x/* modules move as one group. They are released together by the Go team and require each other (x/net requires x/text, x/crypto and x/term require x/sys), so `go mod tidy` after bumping one often bumps another anyway, and two PRs would conflict on go.sum. Coherence plus churn reduction. Every x/ module is v0, so this effectively never sees a major. Applies to direct and indirect requires alike (labelprint's x/image and x/text are both indirect). Matched by the `go` datasource so a same-named path in another ecosystem cannot join. It sets no automerge of its own: non-major bumps inherit automerge.json's bundle rule, which this rule follows in every consumer's extends order.

The Go toolchain moves as ONE PR: the `golang` Docker image (a Dockerfile build stage), go.mod's `go` and `toolchain` directives (gomod, depName and packageName `go`, datasource golang-version), and setup-go's `go-version:` input (github-actions, depName `go`, packageName `actions/go-versions`; setup-go-faster maps to the same package). Split, the halves break the build: the golang image sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, so a go.mod that asks for a newer Go than the image ships fails `go: go.mod requires go >= X.Y.Z (running go X.Y.W; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)`, and a CI job that reads `go-version-file: go.mod` would test a different Go than the image builds. `actions/go-versions` is PRE-SEEDED: labelprint passes `go-version-file`, which Renovate does not extract. A two-part `go-version: '1.27'` gets a one-time `pin` to the exact triple on THIS branch (default.json's top-level `rangeStrategy: pin`; seen in a dry run as `1.27 -> 1.27.3 [pin] renovate/go-toolchain`). That is DELIBERATE and differs from python.json's `replace` for `uv python install`: the point of this group is that CI tests exactly the Go the image ships, and a floating `1.27` resolves to whatever patch setup-go finds at run time. `internalChecksFilter: none` KEEPS BOTH HALVES ON ONE VERSION, as for python.json's `python runtime`: golang-version dates a release by Go's release day, and Docker Hub dates the image by `tag_last_pushed`, which every base rebuild restarts. Go 1.27.3 shipped 2026-10-19, and Docker Hub dated `golang:1.27.3-alpine` 2026-11-06T01:23Z. Under the default `strict`, a fixture branch paired `golang:1.27.2-alpine` (the newest image that had soaked) with `go 1.27.3`. Under `none` every half targets the newest release, and `renovate/stability-days` stays pending until each has met its own soak, which blocks automerge. That is safe only together with the image exemption below (see it). DOCKERFILE BASES: docker.json's `dockerfile bases` rule negates `golang` and `docker.io/library/golang`. Consumers extend :go before :docker, and without that negation the later preset would win the image's groupName and pull it out of this group. Keep this list, the minor gate, the image exemption and that negation in sync. COMMIT TYPE `deps:` IS LOAD-BEARING once a workflow line is a member: default.json types every github-actions dep `ci:`, and a branch takes the highest-priority type among its upgrades (`deps` is unranked), so ONE setup-go line would retype a Go bump of the shipped binary `ci:`, which release-drafter hides. Same trade as python.json: a branch of only workflow lines also releases. MATCHED BY DATASOURCE too (`docker`, `golang-version`, `github-releases`), so an apk `go` package (Alpine ships one) or a mise/asdf `go` tool cannot inherit this group's `internalChecksFilter: none` or the minor gate's labels. NO `matchUpdateTypes`: a minor joins the group too, and so does the image's FIRST `pinDigest` (python.json's group shares this): an adopter's tag->digest conversion rides this branch instead of `pins`. PATCHES STALL WHILE A MINOR IS HELD: `separateMinorPatch` stays off fleet-wide, so a 1.27.x patch and 1.28.0 share the `non-major` bucket, and under `internalChecksFilter: none` the branch always targets the newest release. From the day 1.28.0 appears, `renovate/go-toolchain` is the manual minor PR and no 1.27.x patch opens on its own. Go ships N and N-1 security releases together, so the image misses them until that PR is merged, and no OSV PR fills the gap (stdlib advisories reach only a `toolchain` line, below). Merge the minor PR promptly after review; Trivy is the backstop. The minor gate below makes it manual, and Go has no majors (a 2.0 is not on any roadmap). KNOWN GAP, NOT FIXED: Renovate maps OSV's Go `stdlib` advisories onto the `toolchain` directive only, and `vulnerabilityAlerts` forces `groupName: security updates`, so in a repo with a `toolchain` line a stdlib CVE opens a security PR that moves that line and leaves the image behind. labelprint has no `toolchain` line; its image follows on the normal schedule. LIBRARIES: bumping the `go` directive raises every downstream module's floor. No fleet repo is a Go library; one would disable depType `golang`.

A Go MINOR (`1.27.x` -> `1.28.0`) is reviewed like a major: `automerge: false`, a 7-day soak, and the `breaking`/`needs-review` labels. WHY: Go has no majors, so the X.Y release is the one that changes behavior. The Go 1 promise keeps the language compatible, but a `go` line bump flips GODEBUG defaults (behavior keyed off the go.mod line, e.g. net/http, crypto/x509, crypto/tls settings), and an x.y.0 is usually followed by an x.y.1 within weeks. Twice a year, so the review is cheap. Without this rule, automerge.json's bundle gives a minor `automerge: true` like any other non-major. PATCHES keep automerging: an X.Y.Z release is a bugfix/security release. The 7-day soak lands on the golang-version and setup-go halves; the image exemption below puts the image back to `0 days`. Under the group's `internalChecksFilter: none` the PR opens at once and the soak shows as a pending `renovate/stability-days` check. ONE NON-AUTOMERGE HALF IS ENOUGH: `generateBranchConfig` sets the branch's automerge to `every(upgrade.automerge)` and unions `addLabels`. `vulnerabilityAlerts` still automerges a security fix, because it is applied as `force`. Same names and datasources as the group rule above.

Exempt the `golang` Docker IMAGE in a Dockerfile `FROM` from `minimumReleaseAge`; the golang-version half (go.mod's directives) carries the soak. WHY: Docker Hub dates a tag by `tag_last_pushed`, the LATEST push, and official images are re-pushed under the same tag on every base rebuild, which restarts the clock (`golang:1.27.3-alpine` dated 2026-11-06, 18 days after Go 1.27.3). In a busy week the image never reaches 3 days, so its age measures base churn, not how long the release has been out. The image only repackages a Go release whose own soak runs on golang-version, and both halves share one branch, so `renovate/stability-days` still stays pending until that release is 3 days old (7 for a minor). SAFE ONLY TOGETHER WITH the group's `internalChecksFilter: none`: under `strict`, an exempt image is never pending while a fresh directive is, so Renovate would drop the go.mod half and open an image-only PR. That PR builds (the old `go` line is still satisfied) but leaves CI on the old Go. test/go-runtime.mjs runs both timelines. SCOPE: `matchManagers: [dockerfile]` + `matchDatasources: [docker]`, so a golang image used as a docker-compose service or a job `container:` keeps the soak. Such an image still JOINS the group, and its re-dated tag can then hold the whole branch's `renovate/stability-days` pending in a busy week; no consumer does this today. Must come AFTER the minor gate above, which it overrides for the image only. Digest refreshes are exempt too, which is intended: a re-push IS a new digest and has the same re-dating problem.
